## Fixed

`structured` markdown now reads the pages that previously needed `pdftotext`,
found by running both over five cities' documents (373 PDFs) and comparing the
results.

- A font that declares a character box several times its type size (10.5 pt
  text in a 58 pt box) placed every line of it up or down the page, so a
  paragraph's first line was read into the heading above it. Such a box is
  now rebuilt around the character's baseline.
- A column of labels down the left of the text (DESCRIPTION & CONTEXT,
  BUILDING TYPES, SITE DESIGN) was spliced into the paragraphs' first lines.
  It is read row by row: each label, then the paragraph beside it.
- A line opening with a section label (`SEC. 520`, `Article IV`, `§ 36-520`)
  starts a heading of its own under another heading line, and a label printed
  alone (`Appendix C`) is a heading line of its own over its title.
- A page of codes, times and capitals whose words are words (a code's
  supplement page list, a bus timetable) is no longer skipped as unreadable.
- A scan carrying a scanner's hidden OCR layer is read both ways, and the
  reading that is more words than fragments is kept: a clean hidden layer
  (text laid sideways, italics OCR runs together) stays, and the page is not
  marked `ocr`; a garbled one still gives way to OCR. `--ocr all` always uses
  OCR.
- A page is read in the frame its text is upright in. A page whose `/Rotate`
  stands text that runs along the page on end (a landscape brochure bound in a
  portrait document) read one letter per line.
- Notes typed onto the page (free-text annotations, such as a cover's
  "Adopted as Regulation, October 12, 2009") are read into `markdown`. `spans`
  stay the text layer.
- A word broken across lines at a hyphen keeps it: `single-family`, not
  `singlefamily`. A typesetter's break then reads `exam-ple`; no letter is
  lost.

The text bench stays at 1204 of 1204 checks, every text-corpus page and all
fourteen reviewed dossiers are unchanged, and the inspect routing flag still
reads a page as displayed.
